record_notes.DCP-LETT-1384: Incomplete April 8, 1851 letter, date established by postmark, containing twenty-three blocks of page-specific criticisms of Lyell third edition. Includes denudation and alluvium, Glen Roy, Coquimbo and South American Tertiaries, taxonomy wording, Permian coverage, volcanic field instruction, cleavage/foliation, Yaquil withdrawal and metals. Book pages are not composition dates. All thirty editorial notes read: later fourth/fifth edition changes, Lyell marginal signs and 1854/1855 discoveries are not Darwin April 1851 knowledge. Raw P9 reads 42 with superscript o and 1620 with no explanatory unit or recovered fractional structure; retain uncertainty rather than repair. No surviving personal incoming prompt is identified; book critique is not automatically a dialogue with a cover letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1502: February 15 with supplied 1853 year. Agassiz gift duplicated a copy already possessed; return by carrier is promised. Adams pamphlets have arrived but are expressly unread, despite expectation of heterodoxy. Later heavily annotated copy does not backdate full reading to receipt. Reports just-completed Alcippe dissection and twelve males, retaining suspected extreme reduction. Prior 1337 received-book witness and later 1850 notebook reading remain distinct; no surviving Lyell covering note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1508: March 24 with supplied 1853 year. Explores viscid lava, common reservoirs, cracks and high-pressure boiler analogy while admitting ignorance and recalled Hopkins uncertainty; asks Lyell to foreground continental elevation. N.B. says the earlier letter Lyell claimed to have sent yesterday did not arrive, not that no current Lyell communication exists. Replying letter itself is unlocated. Summary cites Dana 1850 but detailed apparatus identifies Dana 1852 case; preserve source-version discrepancy. Later June 1853 published adoption and April meeting attendance are not already accomplished events.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1518: June 7 with supplied 1853 year. Found pamphlets and maple sugar at brother home on recent London visit; exact receipt day not stated. Full account of June 1 Geological Society meeting distinguishes Sutherland paper read only in abstract, oral confirmation of angular stones, Trimmer/Murchison dispute, Hopkins qualified agreement and Chambers ice-sheet argument. Did not attend Royal Society election battle, knows reported result. Emma away and July 1 Isle of Wight plan prospective; actual later Eastbourne trip differs. Long later Elizabeth biography in apparatus is not contemporary Darwin knowledge. No incoming letter text identifies pamphlet cover or travel news.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1553: February 18 with supplied 1854 year. Explicitly saw Lyell-to-Horner geological letter two days since, a February 16 reading witness for that third-party communication, not a direct incoming Darwin prompt. Responds to inclination/valley observations and asks about dike width. Museum observations, Ramsay report and Jones report about Prestwich have distinct channels; suspected appropriation is not established, and later published attribution clarifies it. Hooker book published/dedicated, barnacle proofs at page 112, Henslow health feared rather than diagnosed. P5 reports long Australian shipmate letter; footnote identifies Covington, but preserved Covington records are all Darwin outgoing and cannot be substituted for missing incoming text. Later Lyell February 21 and February 23 club reading are not the February 16 source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1626: January 10 with supplied 1855 year. Missing Lyell letter received yesterday, January 9, followed by delayed answer due to business. Strongly defends segregation versus deposition while doubting Sharpe grand curves and seeking confirmation. Initially cannot find Sharpe paper; P3 reports found it with nothing to add, preserving within-letter access progression. Clay-slate derivation is suspicion; metamorphism example and Ascension invitation are arguments, not final consensus. Children recovering and proposed London house remain contemporaneous circumstances. Later March edition changes are apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1630: January 14 with supplied 1855 year. House-hunting January 12–13 delayed response; hopes house secured but is not sure, contrary to editorial summary saying found. Grampian source remembered as read or heard from Sharpe, with apparatus identifying a geographic mismatch; no forced certainty. Distinguishes association from overlying and demands dip as well as strike evidence. Verified raw MathML is four and one-half feet, not 412 feet. Full enclosed sketch viewed: shallow strata/quartz layers crossed by steeper foliation, with labels and quartz folia. It depicts proposed molecular redistribution, not proof of all geology. Some gneiss may be fluid; not all. Missing Lyell objection is not supplied by Darwin January 10 letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1633: Sunday within January 21–February 11, 1855 XML range; calendar candidates are January 21/28 or February 4/11, without one established day. Lyell letter forwarded from Down and now received; exact arrival unknown. Concedes serious gap: parallel foliation/cleavage was assumed distinct from bedding where that cannot be proved. Recalled earlier curve idea and tuff crystallisation case remain author claims. Actual P4 diagram shows quartz nodules and feldspar crystals in parallel layers, with no quantitative scale. Sorby paper not yet obtained. Conditional P.S. distinguishes metamorphosed clay-slate cleavage from other rocks stratification, not a settled universal resolution. Later published consensus not activated here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1672: April 23, 1855 incoming Lyell letter advocates Barrande foreign membership and endorses Dana. Distinguishes published merit from unpublished discoveries Lyell personally saw; thirty gastropod genera/150 species and 150 bivalves are Lyell reported evidence, with claim about Forbes polarity qualified nearly overturned. Proposed Cambrian terminology and French support are current opinion, not later uncontested history. No preceding Darwin letter survives to pair this reverse response. No automatic receipt on composition/council day. Independently located June 10 Darwin-to-Huxley 1697 explicitly encloses this old Lyell note in the same Barrande/Dana campaign, establishing a conservative known-by witness then. Later election failure and Dana 1884 election remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1697: June 10 with supplied 1855 year. Independently read additional witness in full. Asks Huxley to speak for Barrande and Dana at next council if Darwin cannot attend, explicitly enclosing an old Lyell note; footnote identifies April 23 source 1672 and shared dual candidature plus Barrande primordial work confirms it. Conditional request not to answer if attending does not prove attendance. Huxley lecture abstract has been read with disappointment; exact title identity is apparatus and missing cover note remains missing. Upcoming marriage congratulations are not proof wedding already occurred. Later June 14 and July 21 events separate. This source is not a reply to Lyell but uses his incoming evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1277: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Friday evening, conjectural December 7, 1849. Continues a dialogue with missing Lyell reaction, not an incoming text supplied by Darwin own 1275. Reconsiders fissure flows, gases, scoria, slope estimates and denudation while qualifying Dana evidence. Now discusses subsidence arguments and map in detail, whereas 1275 had not reached that chapter; preserve this reading progression without certifying every chapter read. Criticizes reported atoll elevation and representations of his own theory, with quoted and attributed third-party language. Desires another Scottish examination, not an accomplished trip. Questioned date prevents automatic exact December 7 knowledge activation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1287: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Thursday evening assigned January 3, 1850. Has read unpublished Lyell craters paper and heard abbreviated Society reading on December 19. Referee role is editorial inference; recommends maps and exact revisions. Raw HTML splits the numerical example across P1–3 with stray diag/ramme text: the argument is 213 minus 195 equals 18 fathoms or 108 feet, but no intact HTML table preserves original layout. Hold faithful rendering rather than silently repairing body. Explains hollow narrow tuff streams with 25–30 degree inclinations; separates crater-origin dispute from incidental elevation of strata. Accepts several denudation craters but remains doubtful about Palma entrance mechanism. Reopened sealed letter adds P8 about T diagram; no independent later day is supplied. Future printed revisions and Forbes next paper remain distinct. Incoming manuscript is not preserved as an incoming personal letter here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1308: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Friday assigned March 8, 1850. Received and read Lyell presidential address sooner than expected; February 15 delivery does not date Darwin reading. Praises Murchison criticism and clock metaphor, anticipates future organic hour-hand address. Missing private account of anniversary dinner supplies Mahon compliment and Bunsen speech; Darwin recalls a separate 1836 Herschel conversation. Health deterioration restricts London travel and barnacle work progresses slowly. Raises a new Scania/Denmark Lower Cretaceous query from specimen labels and von Buch, requesting optional answer by Lady Lyell. No preserved incoming text supplies those missing private communications.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1337: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Saturday assigned June 8, 1850. Own ripple observations 6–10 feet below low water are distinct from Siau report of 60–70 feet. Width-depth relationship is a conjecture he cannot yet establish. Parker work found at brother house has uncertain bibliographic identity. Emma thanks Lady Lyell for missing news note; Darwin thanks Lyell for approval of his paper. P4 first sentence about Agassiz Lake Superior book is Darwin, followed within the same paragraph by editorial heading From Emma Darwin to M. E. Lyell. P5–6 are Emma, including tickets, hippopotamus, future Tuesday Malvern trip and Katharine pregnancy. Character-level split required. Book received by this letter, but subsequent August reading witness must not be backdated. Later journey and October birth remain future apparatus.

Viewed labelled sketch: comparatively shallow strata and two quartz layers are crossed by steep foliation lines, some marked as folia of pure quartz. Lines and lens-like patches depict the proposed movement of material discussed in P5; no scale or numerical movement distance is encoded. The image is physically attached to the closing paragraph, not to P5 in the DOM.

Viewed long horizontal banded sketch with small rounded nodules labelled nodules of quartz in upper layer, and elongate patches plus short block-like marks labelled crystals of Feldspar in lower layers. It illustrates P4 claimed tuff-to-crystal sequence; it supplies no scale or separately dated observation.

reading_method: Nine targets and additional Huxley witness independently read in full, including XML date attributes, all body/notes/bibliography, raw MathML and two actual figures. Four prior contexts reused with accepted note/ledger/source pins and prior viewed 1287 diagram. Primary independently scanned canonical Covington directions and Lyell/Barrande witness content.

additional_probe_reviewed.limitation: Root verified all six preserved Covington-authority records are Darwin outgoing; absence is bounded by preserved sources, not every archive.
